files.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. EDIT this approved paper-cloak character sheet. User requests a VERY LONG CLOAK. Lengthen the existing wraparound paper cloak dramatically, preserving its closed overlapping front and full coverage around chest, belly, sides and back. In both idle poses the cloak now descends from shoulders ALL THE WAY TO THE ANKLES AND GROUND, hiding nearly all legs, with only the small tips of feet visible below a front opening. The back hem extends beyond floor contact into a clearly visible trailing paper train lying behind the character, approximately half the character's full standing height in length. This must unmistakably look floor-length and trailing, not knee-length or a short cape. Long vertical folded paper planes taper from the shoulders then sweep softly toward the ground, a restrained slender flowing silhouette. In running pose the same extra-long cloak streams far behind, approximately one full body height horizontally, in two or three broad continuous flowing folded planes; it STILL wraps and covers the torso at the front. An opening near the front hem shows one stepping foot and enough leg to communicate running. Preserve same small round head, one dark dot eye, no other facial features, lean body underneath, monochrome chalk-ivory paper material, warm-gray shadows, subtle fibrous matte relief and dark charcoal background. Preserve original three-view layout: large right-facing three-quarter idle left, small right-facing side idle upper right, run lower right. Allow enough room for the long train in every view without clipping or overlapping the other poses; slightly reposition poses as needed. Keep heads approximately the same scale as reference. Cloak collar and overlapping wrap construction stay the same, but elongate front, side AND back panels. Paper not fabric: broad fold creases, softly worn irregular torn-paper hem; no spikes, many thin ribbons or excessive shredded scraps. No hood, scarf, belt, jewelry, armor, weapons, colors, glow, new facial features, extra figures, text or labels. Polished non-pixel 2D game concept. Full garment visible within canvas.

Use case: compositing. EDIT IMAGE 2, the five-panel gameplay environment comparison. IMAGE 1 is the NEW approved character with an EXTREMELY LONG WRAPAROUND PAPER CLOAK. Replace the short cloaks on all FIVE existing heroes in image 2 with the exact floor-length trailing cloak from image 1. Preserve the characters' head size, standing height, one dot eye, chalk ivory material, exact location on the floor, and right-facing direction. Long folded ivory paper panels cover the chest, belly, sides, back AND almost all legs down to ground, with just foot tips visible at the front. A distinct train of paper extends leftward along the ground behind each character, roughly half the character's total height in horizontal length. This visibly long trailing train is essential in every panel. Do not accidentally retain thigh-length cloaks or fully exposed legs. Same overlapping front panels, folded collar, pale warm-gray paper shadows and gently torn hem as image 1. Thin matte paper, broad folds, no fabric weave, no hoods, belts, jewelry, new colors or added props. The figures remain small at the same approximate total heights as image 2; the cloak grows in length, the character does not grow larger. Preserve the exact FIVE-panel layout and existing scenery: top left paper cavern, top right graphite mine, middle left wood, middle right roots, bottom wide wood-to-root transition. Keep all background darkness, foreground terrain contours, colors, charcoal gutters and camera crops as closely unchanged as possible. Let trains rest on the existing uneven ground without burying them inside terrain. One character per panel only. No text, labels, UI, glow, new lighting or scenery. Square concept comparison composite, polished non-pixel 2D illustration.
